research.heading: Research
paragraphs: I am a senior at Swarthmore College majoring in Computer Science and Cognitive Science. My research examines decision-making under uncertainty at three levels: how animals learn to categorize sounds, how people assess risk when using AI systems, and how faithfully large language models reproduce the behavior of human populations.

I work with [Prof. Sukrit Venkatagiri](https://www.sukritv.com/) on human-centered AI safety. My senior thesis, advised by [Prof. Joshua Goldwyn](https://www.swarthmore.edu/joshua-goldwyn), develops reinforcement-learning models of auditory decision-making using behavioral data from the [Geffen Lab](https://hosting.med.upenn.edu/hearing/) at the University of Pennsylvania.

directions.title: Auditing LLM social simulation
directions.text: Quantifying where LLM-based social simulators diverge from real populations, and which errors persist regardless of model fitting.

directions.title: Human-centered AI safety
directions.text: Designing systems that help people reason about scams, privacy, and security trade-offs when using or building with AI.

directions.title: Computational models of learning
directions.text: Reinforcement-learning models that distinguish stimulus learning from reward-independent choice repetition.

items.title: ScamPilot: Simulating Conversations with LLMs to Protect Against Online Scams
items.description: Simulated scam conversations that teach people to recognize and respond to online scams.

items.title: Social simulation audit

items.title: Reinforcement-learning models of auditory categorization learning
items.description: Reinforcement-learning models of auditory categorization, fit to mouse behavior from the [Geffen Lab](https://hosting.med.upenn.edu/hearing/) at Penn.

items.title: PromptSafe: multi-agent deliberation for end-user developers

items.imageAlt: PromptSafe panel: agents for privacy, security, misuse and other viewpoints debate a feature, with a moderator and a "Clash" round in progress.
